note: ✅ ERIK 2026-10-04: "Every reach and distinct people should have at least one gladiator, if not a whole bench. The coliseum is central in the culture here." SNG-669 · THE BENCH. The Great Coliseum's roster by reach: `heads` are the reach's existing champions (the eight cell champions, Saehara, Kesh Ardent), `challengers` are contenders and novices, one at least for every region of the world. Each challenger is a duel opponent in the saehara_challengers shape (concept, style, voiceHints, duelStakes) plus `reach`, `people`, `families` (the function families its practice draws from, for the blind grid's four), `rank` and `record`. No arc: this pool is read by the Coliseum, not by recurrence.
_coverage: Every region but the Crossing has at least one bench member; the Crossing's own is Saehara. Peoples fielded beyond human: valleyfolk, precursor-construct, glade-born, djinn, ent, fae, minotaur, gorgon, keener, revenant, dwarven, elven, merfolk, saltfolk, selkie, drowned sunfolk, boreborn (SNG-670/671: every pocket fields its own).

heads._note: the Stillhold sits inside the Riven Marches
Saehara the Undefeated, the Coliseum's own; his challengers are the saehara_challengers pool

challengers.name: Corra Wade of Millbrook
challengers.concept: A millhand who came to the Crossing with a flail she uses for threshing and has never once apologised for. The valley's crowd comes to see her lose and stays to watch her not.
challengers.style: threshing-flail and a farmer's patience; she outlasts rather than outfights
challengers.voiceHints: Short sentences, a laugh at the wrong moment, calls everyone 'love'.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Patience, of Archive Hollow
challengers.concept: A Precursor construct that walked out of Archive Hollow, registered at the Coliseum under the only name anyone has called it, and has been learning to fight by watching. It does not yet understand why the crowd cheers.
challengers.style: a guard copied from whoever it last lost to, improving bout by bout
challengers.voiceHints: Speaks rarely, in complete and slightly too formal sentences; asks the crowd questions.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Thistle, glade-born
challengers.concept: Glade-born from below Harmonic Heights, who fights to the echo of the arena itself: she hears your step come back off the far wall before you take it.
challengers.style: barefoot, light, always circling toward the loud side of the sand
challengers.voiceHints: Hums. Answers a question with the note it was asked in.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Nyx Harrow, Who Fights With the Lamps Out
challengers.concept: An Umbral who asks, every bout, that the sand-lamps be put out. The Coliseum refuses, every bout, and she wins anyway, eyes closed.
challengers.style: eyes shut, a short blade, sees by other means
challengers.voiceHints: Low, unhurried, says your name as if she has always known it.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Qadir Glassborn
challengers.concept: A djinn out of the Radiant Wastes who fights in a glare he makes himself. The front rows wear smoked glass when he is on the card.
challengers.style: a blade of light that does not diffuse, swung from inside the brightest spot on the sand
challengers.voiceHints: Grand, generous, a showman who means every word; tips the sand-sweepers.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Old Hornbeam
challengers.concept: A Rootkin wrestler from Grovehome who seems to grow a little over the course of a bout, and a little more over a season. Nobody has thrown him in the last third of a fight.
challengers.style: grappling, rooted, slow to start and impossible to finish
challengers.voiceHints: Talks about weather and seasons; never about the fight.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Isk the Perfect Form
challengers.concept: A Somatic from the High Temple of the Body for whom a bout is a recital. She would rather lose beautifully than win ugly, and has never had to choose.
challengers.style: open-handed, flowing, every strike a finished shape
challengers.voiceHints: Precise and warm; corrects your stance kindly, mid-bout.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Tamsin Twice-Thrown
challengers.concept: Churnfolk from Spindrift Hollow who has never fought the same way twice and does not believe it is possible to. The bookmakers hate her.
challengers.style: whatever the moment suggests; she changes weapons between rounds
challengers.voiceHints: Laughs, contradicts herself, means both.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Greaveroot
challengers.concept: An ent of the Deepwood who agreed to one bout a century ago to settle a question, and has stayed because the question keeps coming back. His bouts end at sundown, by his rule and nobody else's.
challengers.style: immovable; lets you exhaust yourself on bark
challengers.voiceHints: Very slow speech; long pauses; occasionally answers last week's question.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Seven-Ascending
challengers.concept: A Lattice-City citizen who enters with a written plan for the bout and executes it to the second. Two losses, both to people who did not do what anyone should.
challengers.style: scheduled, exact, guard always where the plan says it should be
challengers.voiceHints: Polite, unsettling, refers to the bout by its tier and minute.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Cass Ratchet
challengers.concept: An Enginewright from Pressureholt who fights in a rig she built, and rebuilds between rounds. The Coliseum's rules on what counts as a weapon were rewritten twice because of her.
challengers.style: a pressure-rig with a hammer arm, tuned between rounds
challengers.voiceHints: Talks to the rig, not to you. Swears in gauge readings.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: The Lampless Sister
challengers.concept: A Numinous from the Lampless Hermitage who may not be entirely present. Opponents report fighting someone a step to the left of where she stands.
challengers.style: barely there; turns your strike aside with a word
challengers.voiceHints: Whispers. Finishes your sentence, wrongly.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Hedda Plainspoken
challengers.concept: A Verist from the Told Ground who announces every blow before she throws it, and still lands most of them. The crowd counts along.
challengers.style: a maul, called aloud, thrown exactly as named
challengers.voiceHints: Says exactly what is so. 'Left shoulder.' 'You are tired.' 'I am going to win.'
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Velvet Asks
challengers.concept: A fae of the Descent who offers every opponent a better fight before the bell, for a price that is always slightly more than it sounds. Most refuse. The ones who accept remember it.
challengers.style: a whip and an offer; fights warmly and to the hilt
challengers.voiceHints: Velvet-voiced, affectionate, always asking what you want.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Brother Caliel of the Lower Court
challengers.concept: A Seraphic brother who refuses to strike anyone on the ground and has lost three bouts for it. He considers those his best.
challengers.style: shield and mace, luminous, merciful past the point of sense
challengers.voiceHints: Gentle, certain, a little condescending; blesses the sand before he steps on it.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Haldor Bedrock-Born
challengers.concept: A minotaur Mason from Bedrock who insists the sand be weighed before every bout, and once refused to fight on ground that was three pounds light.
challengers.style: horns, a stone-headed hammer, and ground he has tested with his own hooves
challengers.voiceHints: Deep, deliberate, distrusts anything he cannot touch, including compliments.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Sythe of the Figure-Works
challengers.concept: A gorgon Figurist whose gaze freezes a pattern, never a person: the Coliseum's oldest special rule. She stops your next move in its idea before you make it.
challengers.style: veiled until the bell, then the gaze; fights the shape of your intent
challengers.voiceHints: Speaks in figures; finds you interesting, which is not reassuring.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Marten Slowhand
challengers.concept: An Hourkeeper who wins on the bell more often than anyone living. He knows exactly how long is left, and fights as if he has already seen the end.
challengers.style: a quarterstaff and a clock in his head; never in a hurry
challengers.voiceHints: Speaks slowly, in the past tense about things that have not happened yet.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Ender Nell
challengers.concept: An Unmaker from the Scouring who ends a bout the way her people end anything: cleanly, without cruelty, and a little sooner than you were ready for.
challengers.style: two short blades, a clean stop, nothing wasted
challengers.voiceHints: Calm, kind, a little sad; thanks you at the end.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Liss the Keener
challengers.concept: A keener from Wellspring who sings the bout as she fights it. The grief in it is real; the crowd weeps; opponents lose their footing in it.
challengers.style: a long knife and a keening song that rises with the fight
challengers.voiceHints: Sings more than she speaks. When she speaks, it is to ask who you have lost.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Fenn the Lamp-Guide
challengers.concept: A Dusklow guide who takes people down into the dark for a living and treats the sand like a stair: one careful step, then another, then the one you did not see.
challengers.style: a lantern-pole and a guide's sense of footing
challengers.voiceHints: Discreet, wry, keeps your confidences and his own.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Tobin Patch
challengers.concept: A Gearsflat salvager who fixes his kit mid-bout with whatever is to hand, including, once, a piece of his opponent's.
challengers.style: salvaged armour, a wrench, and an inexhaustible supply of wire
challengers.voiceHints: Cheerful, oily, always asking if you are using that.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Rowan Neither-Side
challengers.concept: A Greenmarch forager who will not be told which side of anything they are on, including which corner of the sand. Fights from wherever the opponent is not.
challengers.style: a forager's hook-knife, quick feet, no fixed corner
challengers.voiceHints: Friendly, evasive, changes the subject to mushrooms.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Mattock Greave
challengers.concept: A Greyhearth gravedigger who digs in, literally: he plants a spade-blade in the sand and fights from beside it. He has buried two former opponents, at their request, years later.
challengers.style: a spade, a lot of shoulder, all the time in the world
challengers.voiceHints: Quiet, courteous, measures you with his eyes for something.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Corwin Who Came Back
challengers.concept: A Hardline revenant who trains in the yard where marchers and stillholders train together, and who once lost a bout so badly he did not get up for a year. He came back for the rematch. He won.
challengers.style: marcher forms, a stillholder's patience, and no particular fear of the end
challengers.voiceHints: Flat, dry, a gallows joke about every wound.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Wick Assayer
challengers.concept: A Kindlerow lamp-maker who treats light as a trade: flash-pans, mirrors, a shuttered lantern that opens at exactly the wrong moment for you.
challengers.style: a lamp-hook and a satchel of flash-pans
challengers.voiceHints: Brisk, practical, quotes prices.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Pell Farrow, Just Arrived
challengers.concept: A Longshore outfitter who is always about to leave, including mid-bout. Opponents chase him around the sand and lose on the bell.
challengers.style: a walking-staff and a traveller's stamina
challengers.voiceHints: Always just arrived or about to go; asks where you are headed.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Arbiter Joss
challengers.concept: A Plainstead arbitrator who fights to a decision, not a knockout. She wins on the judges' count more than anyone, and the judges are scared of her.
challengers.style: sword-and-buckler, textbook, scored
challengers.voiceHints: Measured, fair, slightly bored; cites precedent.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: The One Called Nike
challengers.concept: Of the God-Named who hold court at Stair Hollow, she wears the name of victory and has the record to make it hard to argue. The one loss is the bout everyone at the Crossing still talks about.
challengers.style: spear and a borrowed radiance; fights as if the outcome were already written
challengers.voiceHints: Regal, warm, refers to herself by the name; wants to be addressed, not believed.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Doss Terms-Aloud
challengers.concept: A Low Market bargainer who names the terms of his own loss before the bell: what he will pay, what he will concede, what he will never do. Then he keeps every word, whichever way it goes.
challengers.style: a cudgel and a ledger; fights to the letter of what he said
challengers.voiceHints: Courteous, exact, writes things down; offers you a better rate.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Breaker Una
challengers.concept: A Worn Yard demolisher who takes your guard apart the way her crew takes a building apart: properly, in order, load-bearing pieces last.
challengers.style: a pry-bar and a demolisher's eye for what is holding everything up
challengers.voiceHints: Professional, blunt, narrates what she is taking off you next.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Selk the Listener
challengers.concept: A Thinwater pattern-reader who listens to the bout rather than watching it, and hears the opening before it opens.
challengers.style: a staff and a listening stillness
challengers.voiceHints: Soft, attentive, asks you to stop talking so she can hear.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Brannoc Ironvein of the Anvilhall
challengers.concept: The Anvilhall's champion, who forged his own hammer and has refused every offer to buy it. He fights like a hold: everything behind a wall, and then the gate opens.
challengers.style: hammer and a tower shield, armour he made himself
challengers.voiceHints: Gruff, proud of his work, judges your gear before he judges you.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Maeve Stonecount
challengers.concept: A tunneler from the Long Delve who fights at the pace of a nine-hundred-year dig. She has never been rushed, and wins on the bell more often than anyone but Marten Slowhand.
challengers.style: a mattock and endless patience
challengers.voiceHints: Slow, dry, measures time in tunnel-lengths.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Orrin of Greyspire
challengers.concept: A Greyspire warden who learned to fight on the long stair down to the trees, and fights every bout as if someone above him is about to cut the rope.
challengers.style: axe and a climber's footing
challengers.voiceHints: Loud, quick to insult elves, quicker to buy one a drink after.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Hask of the Deep Stone
challengers.concept: From the kingdom under the Given Land. He insists on fighting on bare stone and has the Coliseum lift a panel of sand for every bout.
challengers.style: stone-knuckled gauntlets and no weapon at all
challengers.voiceHints: Very few words, all of them true; distrusts anything above ground.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Ylva of Undermere
challengers.concept: A lake-boatwoman from Undermere who fights by lamplight and asks the crowd to keep quiet so she can hear the water that is not there.
challengers.style: boat-hook and a lantern on her belt
challengers.voiceHints: Quiet, watchful, speaks of the surface world as 'up there'.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Aelith of the Evenwood
challengers.concept: An Evenwood ranger who rarely lets a blade near her. She counts her three losses as lessons and can tell you exactly what each one taught. The ents taught her to be still; she taught herself the rest.
challengers.style: longknife and stillness, moving only when it matters
challengers.voiceHints: Calm, ancient-sounding, a little amused by everything.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Sylas of the Silverbough
challengers.concept: A Silverbough archer who was told bows were not allowed in the Coliseum and so learned the spear, badly at first and now very well. He will tell you he prefers the bow.
challengers.style: spear, light feet, and a hunter's patience
challengers.voiceHints: Elegant, condescending, devastating at the exact moment you stop listening.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Ithriel of Highmere
challengers.concept: A Highmere envoy who fights as an argument: every exchange a premise, and the last one the conclusion. Figurists come down to the Crossing just to watch.
challengers.style: a slender sword and a mind that is three moves ahead
challengers.voiceHints: Polite, faintly bored, treats the bout as a debate she has already won.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Kael of Windspire
challengers.concept: A Windspire glider-rider who fights as if the sand were a long way down and he had wings. He mostly does not, in the arena. He mostly wins anyway.
challengers.style: twin blades and acrobatics learned on the anchor-chains
challengers.voiceHints: Breezy, reckless, laughs on the way down.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Nerys of the Coral Court
challengers.concept: A merfolk champion who fights in the Coliseum's flooded pit on the full tide, the only bout of the month in water. Land-folk who accept her challenge learn what a current is.
challengers.style: trident and a net, at home in waist-deep water
challengers.voiceHints: Musical, curious about land things, asks what your feet feel like.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Garr Netmender
challengers.concept: A Saltmarch fisherman who fights the way he hauls a net: steady, low, and he does not let go.
challengers.style: a weighted net and a gutting knife
challengers.voiceHints: Plain-spoken, salt-cracked, asks nothing about where you are from.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Moira of the Greywater
challengers.concept: A selkie who comes up from the Greywater Deep for one season of bouts a year and sings for the drowned before each one. She keeps her sealskin in a locked box at the Coliseum, and the key on her.
challengers.style: bare hands, seal-quick, singing
challengers.voiceHints: Soft, sad, wry; asks you who you have lost to the sea.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Jory Hullborn
challengers.concept: Born on a deck of the Tidewrought and never on land until he was twenty. He fights as if the sand were rolling and wins because it is not.
challengers.style: cutlass and a sailor's balance
challengers.voiceHints: Cheerful, salty, homesick for the swell.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Ser Saelor of the Drowned Crown
challengers.concept: A knight of the kingdom under the ocean, who fights in the Coliseum with his helm full of seawater. He has lost four bouts, every one of them on land that was too dry, and he fights for his crown's claim, which the Mavens have not yet recognised.
challengers.style: longsword and drowned plate, slow and certain
challengers.voiceHints: Courtly, archaic, speaks as if from a long way off.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Tala Swellrider
challengers.concept: A leviathan-rider from the Road who came ashore to fight because the leviathan she rides is resting, and she is bored. She has never stood still on anything that was not moving.
challengers.style: harpoon-spear and a rider's balance
challengers.voiceHints: Big laugh, big gestures, talks about her leviathan like a friend.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Wren of Sunfold
challengers.concept: A cutting-crew girl from Sunfold who learned to fight at the Long Noon's edge, against things that grow back. She hits everything twice on principle, and she is still learning that people mostly do not grow back.
challengers.style: a hooked cutting-blade and a farmer's stamina
challengers.voiceHints: Cheerful, sunburnt, keeps asking where the sun is up here.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Garrow Ringhand
challengers.concept: A Boreborn cap-keeper who fights with a ringing-hammer and listens to your guard the way he listens to a cap: for the flat note where it will give.
challengers.style: a long-handled hammer and an oilskin coat
challengers.voiceHints: Few words, all of them about sound. Taps your shield before the bell to hear it.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave

challengers.name: Rafe Slipman of Keelmouth
challengers.concept: A shipwright from the only slipway on four hundred miles of cliff, who fights the way a hull is floated off the mud: patiently, then all at once on the tide.
challengers.style: a caulking mallet and a boat-hook
challengers.voiceHints: Talks in tides and keel-lengths; asks where you were launched.
challengers.duelStakes: prestige: a bout at the Great Coliseum ends at the bell or a yield, never at a grave
